title: Guidelines for Verification of the DDNS Method for Poliovirus Detection
author: Joyce Akello
materials: Analyse the data using the Piranha GUI software.

steps.title: Reconstitute CVA20 control
steps.instruction: In a Class II MSCII, add 1 mL nuclease‑free water (NFW) to the lyophilised CVA20 vial, mix gently by pipetting up‑and‑down until the powder is fully dissolved and any residue on the seal is rinsed in.

steps.title: Prepare 30 µL aliquots
steps.instruction: Aliquot the reconstituted CVA20 into sterile 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes (30 µL each), label each tube with the vial ID and preparation date, keep on ice for immediate use or store at –20 °C (≈33 aliquots per vial).

steps.title: Create ten‑fold dilution series
steps.instruction: Label tubes 10‑1 to 10‑4. Add 270 µL NFW to tubes 10‑2, 10‑3 and 10‑4. Add 270 µL NFW to tube 10‑1 and then add 30 µL of a fresh 10‑1 aliquot (neat control) to label it 10‑1. Mix gently. Transfer 30 µL from 10‑1 into tube 10‑2, mix; transfer 30 µL from 10‑2 into tube 10‑3, mix; transfer 30 µL from 10‑3 into tube 10‑4, mix. This yields a ten‑fold series from neat (10⁰) to 10⁻⁴.

steps.title: Prepare negative extraction control
steps.instruction: Place 300 µL pure NFW into a labelled tube (sample 11) to serve as the extraction negative control.

steps.title: Spike dilutions for Stage 1
steps.instruction: Add each ten‑fold dilution (10‑1 to 10‑4) into separate tubes containing 270 µL NFW, producing ten samples for viral RNA extraction (Stage 1).

steps.title: Prepare duplicate neat controls (Stage 1)
steps.instruction: Add 270 µL NFW to two separate 30 µL aliquots of the neat positive control; label these tubes 1 and 2. These are the duplicate Stage 1 controls.

steps.title: Prepare stool matrix samples (Stage 2)
steps.instruction: Transfer 300 µL of each of five previously tested negative stool suspensions into labelled tubes (Samples 1‑5).

steps.title: Spike stool suspensions
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL of a fresh neat positive‑control aliquot to each of the five stool tubes (270 µL stool), mix gently by pipetting. These are the spiked stool samples for Stage 2.

steps.title: Add assay controls for Stage 2
steps.instruction: Add 270 µL water to one 30 µL positive‑control aliquot (Assay positive control, Sample 11) and add 300 µL PCR‑grade water as the negative control (Sample 12). Total samples for RNA extraction in Stage 2 = 12.

steps.title: Extract viral RNA (Stages 1‑2)
steps.instruction: Using the MagMAX Viral RNA Isolation kit, extract RNA from all prepared samples (Stage 1 and Stage 2) following the small‑volume protocol (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.81wgbzpyogpk/v2). Keep extracted RNA on ice, use immediately for RT‑PCR, and store any leftover RNA frozen.

steps.title: First‑round RT‑PCR
steps.instruction: On the same day as extraction, perform the first‑round RT‑PCR on each RNA extract using the DDNS protocol (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rm7vzbyyx1/v6). Include a PCR negative control that contains NFW instead of RNA.

steps.title: Barcoded VP1 PCR (Stage 1)
steps.instruction: Use the first‑round PCR products as templates for barcoded VP1 PCR, setting up 13 reactions (12 samples + 1 negative control). Assign a unique barcode to each reaction and record the barcode‑sample mapping.

steps.title: Barcoded VP1 PCR (Stage 2)
steps.instruction: Perform barcoded VP1 PCR on all Stage 2 first‑round products, creating 14 reactions (12 samples + 2 negative controls). Use barcodes different from those used in Stage 1 and record the assignments.

steps.title: Gel or Tapestation verification
steps.instruction: Run all VP1 amplicons on a 1.5 % agarose gel (or on a Tapestation if available) to confirm successful amplification.

steps.title: Store amplicons
steps.instruction: Store the verified PCR products in a refrigerator (≈4 °C) or freeze them if a freezer is available, pending sequencing together with amplicons from Stages 1‑3.

steps.title: Stage 3 sample selection
steps.instruction: Identify five stool samples previously confirmed positive and five confirmed negative by virus isolation/ITD‑qPCR. Include an NFW negative control and the CVA20 assay positive control in the run.

steps.title: Extract RNA for Stage 3
steps.instruction: Extract viral RNA from the 12 Stage 3 samples using the MagMAX kit as described above; keep RNA on ice and store leftovers frozen.

steps.title: First‑round PCR (Stage 3)
steps.instruction: Perform the first‑round PCR on each Stage 3 RNA extract (same‑day) using the DDNS protocol, with an NFW negative control.

steps.title: Nested VP1 PCR (Stage 3)
steps.instruction: Run nested (barcoded) VP1 PCR on all Stage 3 first‑round products, assigning barcodes that are distinct from those used in Stages 1 and 2. Record barcode assignments.

steps.title: Verify Stage 3 amplicons
steps.instruction: Run the nested VP1 amplicons on agarose gel or Tapestation to confirm amplification.

steps.title: Store Stage 3 amplicons
steps.instruction: Store the Stage 3 amplicons in the fridge (or freeze) pending sequencing.

steps.title: Handle inhibition in stool samples
steps.instruction: If any spiked stool sample fails to amplify, repeat RNA extraction and barcoded VP1 PCR using a 1:10 dilution of the original stool suspension to assess inhibition.

steps.title: Prepare blinded verification set (Stage 4)
steps.instruction: Create a worksheet listing 5‑10 previously tested stool samples, assign new laboratory IDs, and blind the original results. The senior scientist must perform the blinding.

steps.title: Process blinded samples through DDNS
steps.instruction: Treat the blinded samples exactly as routine specimens: RNA extraction, first‑round RT‑PCR, barcoded VP1 PCR, and gel/Tapestation verification, following the DDNS protocol (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rm7vzbyyx1/v6).

steps.title: Nanopore library preparation and sequencing
steps.instruction: Prepare sequencing libraries from all barcoded VP1 amplicons generated in Stages 1‑3 and the blinded set, pool them, and perform nanopore sequencing according to the DDNS protocol.

steps.title: Sequence data analysis
steps.instruction: Analyse the nanopore data with the Piranha GUI software, perform all required quality‑control checks, and generate run reports.

steps.title: Compile verification report
steps.instruction: Record the results of each stage in the DDNS_Verification_Report_V3.docx template, attach gel images, run reports, and Piranha analysis, and share the complete package with the PSC team for review.

steps.title: Evaluate blinded sample results
steps.instruction: Compare the newly generated results for the blinded samples with the previously obtained results. If any discrepancy occurs, repeat the entire workflow; minor variations near the detection limit may be acceptable after careful evaluation.

steps.title: Finalize QA documentation
steps.instruction: After PSC review, archive the verification report, gel images, sequencing reports, and Piranha QC outputs as part of the laboratory’s quality‑assurance records.
